Various fibers investigated for their cut quality in SMC production ______________________________________________________________ Kaltex (450-600k) – 0.5 and 1 inch cut lengths TE4571150704 (EP 834) - Epoxy sized TU4571140407 (U6-01) - Urethane sized TR4571150907 (U2-01) - Urethane sized TW4571140309 (HL 763) - Water-based polymer Montefibre (300k) - 0.5 inch OC glass fiber Fiberglass – 0.5” and 1” High resolution scanning electron microscopy was used to evaluate the cross-section of the cut fiber(s) and width. We refer to the transverse dimension of the fiber tow(s) as ‘width’. Only when the fiber bundle is fully filamentized to single fiber, then this can be referred to as ‘diameter’. For multiple fibers that agglomerate we measure their collective transverse dimension, which we are calling as width. The fibers were dispersed in a container in which air was blown to disperse and separate the fibers. About 200-300 individual fiber measurements were performed to evaluate fiber length. Figures 25 to 41 are a series of images for each of the above variants and the corresponding statistical evaluation of fiber width. 24 Figure 25.Example of cut cross-section – Kaltex (epoxy sized)- (left) 1” and right (0.5”) Very uniform cut Fiber cross-section evaluation The Kaltex epoxy sized TCF cut very uniformly Figure 25 provides cross-section of the Kaltex carbon fibers which have uniform kidney shape. The cut ends were clean indicating the interaction of the cutting blade with the fiber was optimal. Figure 26.Comparison of precursors in terms of cut quality – 0.5” fiber length. (Left) 0.5” Kaltex, (Right) 0.5” Montefibre Figure 26 compares ½” cut for the Kaltex and Montefibre precursor based TCF. Both materials were effectively cut; however, the 0.5” Monfibre fiber had more rough features on the cross- section, while the Kaltex cut smooth with uniform cross-section. The reason for this variation is thought to be the effect of fiber sizing interaction with the cutter. The sizing type, make-up (composition), thickness are some factors that affect the cut quality. 25 The effect of sizing is further accentuated in comparing epoxy versus urethane sized. It is known that the epoxy size results in a stiffer surface to the TCF, while the urethane size is softer on the TCF surface. Figure 27 compares epoxy versus urethane sized TCF for 0.5” fiber length. The epoxy sized fiber has a uniform clean cross-section. The urethane sized TCF has a rough and serrated cross-section, indicating higher resistance to the cut possibly caused by more fiber compliance (softer) in the cutter section. Figure 27. Sizing effect – Epoxy versus Urethane sizing. (Left) – epoxy sized; (Right – urethane sized TCF The glass fiber cut very clean (and match stick like) and the standard deviation (SD) is very narrow.
